title: GOATED Enforcement Event Model
description: What the enforcement core needs to judge one event, and what it answers (ADR 0004). The root is a request; `$defs/decision` is the answer, and `$defs/scenario_file` a file of conformance scenarios. Calls have kinds, never harness tool names.

version.description: The event model's version: a whole number every change bumps. A request or decision of any other version is refused, not guessed at.

turns.description: Every turn since the last compaction, oldest first; the last is the current turn. Facts that outlast these turns (the task's route, the briefed flag, turn markers, friction counts, spawn brief templates) are the core's own, kept by session id, and never carried here. Empty only at a session start.

agent.description: Who is acting. A subagent's turns are its own; the routing gates do not apply to it and no override reaches it.

folders.description: The project's folders. A file is outside the project only when it is certainly under none of them.

agent_folders.description: The harness's own configuration folders. A write there is never scratch.

installed_skills.description: Skill names the harness can find. Null when the adapter cannot tell.

context_docs.description: The project's own context documents that exist, as paths from the project's root: of `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/agents/context-matrix.md`, and `docs/agents/project-standards.md`, the ones the adapter found. The orientation hold and the closeout note name them. Absent or empty: none.

event.description: The one event to judge. Only a pending call and a turn end can be held; the others answer with notices only.

oneOf.description: A call about to run. It is not yet in the turn's entries.
A call that has just run. It need not be in the turn's entries yet.
A prompt was submitted; it is the opener or last entry of the current turn.

key.description: Stable for the life of the turn, unique in the session.

oneOf.description: A compaction opens a turn of its own.

entries.description: What happened in the turn after its opener, in order.

author.description: person: a person typed it, so it may carry overrides. session: another session or agent sent it, such as a brief or a message. host: the harness wrote it, such as a retry or a background result. unknown: the adapter cannot tell, and it counts as not a person.

text.description: The author's own text, with harness-inserted blocks removed.

pasted.description: Text the person pasted rather than typed. Never read for overrides.

starts_session.description: This is the session's first prompt, a brief from the session that started it. Its route line counts as the first turn's.

oneOf.description: A later prompt that continues the turn rather than opening one, such as a background result or an own subagent's report. It carries no override.

A call, where it was made, with its result once it has finished. A call with no result is still running. Its route and skip lines count here, where it was made; it finished where a call_finished entry names its id, or, with none, here.
Where a call made earlier in the turn finished, for calls that finish in another order than they were made. The result stays on the call's own entry.
A person loaded a skill by name, such as a typed command.
A background agent this session spawned has finished.
The turn's end was allowed. Overrides typed for the turn stop applying; a later continuing prompt keeps its route and lines.

call.description: A call by its kind, one branch per kind. `line_text` is the one field a route or skip line may be read from, for a harness that may not keep reply text whole; leave it out otherwise. `action` is an opaque key the harness may give so that calls the model shows alike, such as spawns by two different tools, count as different actions where the core counts repeated actions.

whole_file.description: The call writes the whole file, creating or replacing it; its one edit's added text is the content, and its removed text is null, since the call does not say what the file held.

creates.description: An edit, not a whole-file write, that makes the file when it is missing, as a harness may let an edit with no removed text do.

edits.description: The call's changes; empty when it changes nothing.

removed.description: The text the edit replaces; null when the call does not say, such as a whole-file write or a notebook cell's replacement.

added.description: The text the edit writes; null when it writes none it can show, such as a deleted notebook cell.

oneOf.description: A shell command. A commit or pull request made by a command stays a shell_command; the core reads the command.

skill.description: The name as the harness gave it, namespace included; the core decides whether it counts.

whole.description: False when the call asked for part of the file.

oneOf.description: Handing work to another agent or session.

starts_now.description: False when the call only proposes the work and nothing runs until a person starts it.

read_only.description: The spawned agent has no write, edit, or shell tool.

separate.description: The agent runs apart from the acting session, as another session does, so its report never comes back as this call's result. A call that only proposes the work starts nothing that reports back either.

oneOf.description: A tool that only records a commit.
A tool that only opens a pull or merge request.

base.description: The branch it merges into, when the call names one.

head.description: The branch it merges from, when the call names one.

repository.description: The repository it is opened in, as owner/name, the owner perhaps a path of groups (group/subgroup/name), when the call names one; a change of another repository is not measured.

ok.description: False when the call failed or was refused.

held.description: A GOATED hold refused it, so it never ran.

ran.description: False when the call never ran for a reason other than a GOATED hold, which `held` says: refused by the harness or another hook, or interrupted. A run that never happened neither fails nor passes a check. Absent means it ran unless held.

agent.description: For a spawn: the agent it started.

background.description: Started in the background; done once an agent_finished entry names it.

entries.description: The agent's own turn, for rules that count its work toward this turn.

allOf.description: A held call never ran, and `held` alone says so.
A call that never ran did not succeed.

skill_name.description: A bare skill name. The marker grammar in stack/fixtures/markers/README.md owns this shape.

holds.description: Every hold the event meets, in the order the gates fire. The first decides how a harness with one reason field shows it.

gate.description: A gate the enforcement contract names; the contract owns the list.

text.description: What the agent must do, shown after the hold line the contract defines.

scenario_file.description: Conformance scenarios: sequences of events, each judged step with the decision it must get. They name no harness.

covers.description: What the scenario proves, for the coverage check: a gate holding, a way it clears (a clear way the contract's Gates table names, shown by the same call held without it), or a near miss it must not hold.

setup.description: The project as the scenario needs it before the first step.

agent.description: Who acts in the steps: the main agent (the default), or a subagent, whose turns are its own and whose prompts its parent sent (author session).

branch_changed_lines.description: The project is a checkout whose branch changes this many lines of non-test code against its base.

origin_url.description: With branch_changed_lines: the URL of that checkout's remote `origin`, which is never fetched.

step.description: One event or entry. A prompt opens a turn unless it continues one; a call is judged before it is recorded; the turn's end and a session start are judged.

continues.description: The prompt continues the current turn as an entry.

oneOf.description: A call: judged as a pending call, then recorded with its result. An absent expect means it must be allowed. expect_after judges it again as a finished call.

The runner, not the agent, adds this many changed lines of non-test code to the project's checkout, as a new untracked code file, so a setup branch grows between steps. Nothing is judged and no adapter sees it as an event.

expectation.description: The decision a step must get. Holds are matched by gate and kind, in firing order; their text is guidance and is not compared. When notices are given, the decision carries exactly those kinds, in any order.

items.description: For a closeout hold: exactly the labels of the items it lists, as the contract's Closeout Items table names them.

kind.description: fail_open: the core could not judge and allowed the event. warning: it judged, but something it reads was missing. override_recorded: a person's override for the turn. closeout_note: the turn's closeout items, early. session_notice: a session-start or friction notice. skip_carried: a read gate let a call through on a skip line that lasts the task. reads_owed: a read gate let a write through before its references were read, which the closeout's Reads item then asks for. route_continued: a person's prompt in a session with a routed task runs as `goated-route: continue`, and says that new work needs a new route line.
